title: Koszul syzygies imply saturation of linear chart relations
statement: Let $S$ be a commutative ring, $s\ge1$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_s,t_2,\ldots,t_s\in S$. In the free module $S^s$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of $s$-tuples let $e_i$ be the standard unit vectors. Assume that every $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_s)\in S^s$ with $\sum_i f_iv_i=0$ can be written as $v=\sum_{i<j}b_{ij}(f_ie_j-f_je_i)$ for coefficients $b_{ij}\in S$. Set $J=(f_1t_i-f_i\mid 2\le i\le s)$ and $Q=S/J$. Then multiplication by the image of $f_1$ on $Q$ is injective. In particular, for every $h\in S$ and integer $N\ge0$, $f_1^Nh\in J$ implies $h\in J$, or equivalently every class $x\in Q$ with $f_1^Nx=0$ is zero.

proof.text: Put $g_i=f_1t_i-f_i$ for $2\le i\le s$. Suppose $f_1h\in J$. By the meaning of the finitely generated ideal $J$, choose $c_2,\ldots,c_s\in S$ with $f_1h=\sum_{i=2}^s c_i g_i$. In the tuple module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] set $v=(h-\sum_{i=2}^s c_it_i,c_2,\ldots,c_s)$. Expanding gives $\sum_{i=1}^s f_iv_i=f_1h-\sum_{i=2}^s c_i(f_1t_i-f_i)=0$. The hypothesis of the item therefore supplies coefficients $b_{ij}$ such that $v=\sum_{i<j}b_{ij}(f_ie_j-f_je_i)$. Define $\lambda:S^s\to S$ by $\lambda(w)=w_1+\sum_{i=2}^s t_iw_i$. Distributing finite sums proves that $\lambda$ is $S$-linear, and substitution of the coordinates of $v$ gives $\lambda(v)=h$.

proof.text: Set $w=(1,t_2,\ldots,t_s)$ and let $\lambda:S^s\to S$ be the linear functional $\lambda(v)=\sum_i w_iv_i=v_1+\sum_{i=2}^s t_iv_i$. Let $q:S\to S/J$ be the quotient map. The defining generators of $J$ give $q(f_i)=q(f_1)q(w_i)$ for every index, including the first index where $w_1=1$. Thus for every pair $i,j$, $q(\lambda(f_ie_j-f_je_i))=q(f_i)q(w_j)-q(f_j)q(w_i)=0$ by commutativity. Consequently every Koszul generator has image under $\lambda$ in $J$. Apply $\lambda$ to the boundary expression of the relation $v$ in Step 1. Closure of $J$ under finite sums and scalar multiplication gives $\lambda(v)\in J$, and direct evaluation gives $\lambda(v)=h$. This proves $f_1h\in J\Rightarrow h\in J$ without cancellation in $S$. When $s=1$, all pair sums are empty and the same proof gives $h=0\in J=(0)$.

proof.text: Every $x\in Q=S/J$ has a representative $h\in S$. If $[f_1]x=0$, then $f_1h\in J$, hence $h\in J$ by Step 2, and $x=0$. If $[f_1]x=[f_1]y$, apply this assertion to $x-y$ to get $x=y$; multiplication by $[f_1]$ is injective. Induct on $N$ to prove that $[f_1]^Nx=0$ implies $x=0$: for $N=0$ the equation is $x=0$; for $N+1$, the zero-kernel assertion applied to $[f_1]^Nx$ gives $[f_1]^Nx=0$, and the induction hypothesis gives $x=0$. Finally $[f_1]^N[h]=[f_1^Nh]$, so this assertion is equivalent to $f_1^Nh\in J\Rightarrow h\in J$.

lean.statement: theorem koszul_relations_quotient_torsionfree {S : Type u} [CommRing S] (n : ℕ) (f : Fin (n + 1) → S) (t : Fin n → S) (hsyzygies : ∀ v : Fin (n + 1) → S, (∑ i, f i * v i) = 0 → ∃ b : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (n + 1) → S, v = ∑ i, ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun j ↦ i < j), b i j • (f i • Pi.single j (1 : S) - f j • Pi.single i (1 : S))) : Function.Injective (fun x : S ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ f 0 * t i - f i.succ)) ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (f 0) * x) ∧ (∀ (h : S) (N : ℕ), f 0 ^ N * h ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ f 0 * t i - f i.succ)) → h ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ f 0 * t i - f i.succ))) ∧ (∀ (N : ℕ) (x : S ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ f 0 * t i - f i.succ))), Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (f 0) ^ N * x = 0 → x = 0)
